newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids hold again despite soft crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids hold again despite soft crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady on Tuesday in slack activity, with some recent interest for utilities propping up the complex despite another crude slide and competitive gas prices, sources said.

"There has been some utility interest, but no one's burning anything and gas is starting to undercut fuel," said one cash trader, adding a couple of big players also were trying to hold up prices near-term.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $16.25-50 a barrel, with 0.3 percent high pour also talked steady in the $16.75-17.00 area, traders said.
New York high sulphurs also were little changed, with three percent still talked on either side of $14.75.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent edged up slightly to $15.50-75, traders said.
USG three percent notionally held flat at about $15, but some thought the high sulphur market was a bit weaker though nothing was done at lower levels.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices slipped about a nickel Tuesday to the $2.45/mmBtu level, or about $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was a few cents lower at about $2.21/mmBtu, or $13.92 a barrel.
